headline: PFAS and bisphenol A toxicity mechanisms mapped by network toxicology and validation
label: Pfas Network Toxicology
summary: Network toxicology paired with experimental validation is now used to map mechanistic pathways of PFAS and bisphenol A toxicity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is network toxicology coupled with experimental validation to resolve mechanisms of exposure-linked organ toxicity. Six of seven items address environmental contaminants: 6:2 Cl-PFESA in non-obstructive azoospermia, PFOS effects on uric acid handling via URAT1 and GLUT9 in HK-2 cells, PFOS precursor-driven lipidomic remodeling in HepaRG cells, PFDA-induced granulosa cell toxicity attenuated by kaempferol, 6PPDQ in steatotic liver disease, and bisphenol A in chronic non-bacterial prostatitis via ITGAX and M1 macrophage polarization. The cyclophosphamide ovarian insufficiency study extends the approach with machine learning, Mendelian randomization and multi-omics, prioritizing CXCL1 and COL4A4 as candidate biomarkers. The new element is the integration of computational prioritization with cell-line and animal validation across reproductive, renal, hepatic, and immune endpoints.
